title: GSF Holds High-Level Meeting With Haiti Ministry of Defense; Security Forces Seize Weapons and Ammunition; Zed Airlines Opens Miami–Cap-Haïtien Route
detail: HaitiLibre's May 23, 2026 Zapping roundup reported three significant developments. First, a high-level strategic coordination meeting was held between Gang Suppression Force (GSF) leadership and Haiti's Ministry of Defense, reflecting growing institutional integration between the international mission and Haitian national security structures. The meeting comes as the GSF's ~800-person advance force (400+ Chadian, 75 Guatemalan, 70 Salvadoran) enters its second full month of operations under Mongolian Maj. Gen. Erdenebat Batsuuri — who assumed command on May 14 — with the force exclusively concentrated in Port-au-Prince city center and far below its authorized 5,500-person ceiling. Second, Haitian National Police (HNP) and security forces conducted operations resulting in the seizure of weapons and ammunition, consistent with ongoing enforcement efforts targeting gang supply chains fueling the ongoing Cité Soleil and Cul-de-Sac violence wave. Specific quantities and operational details were not disclosed for security reasons. Third, Zed Airlines announced the inauguration of a new Miami-to-Cap-Haïtien direct flight route — the first new international air connection to Cap-Haïtien in recent years, representing a rare positive economic development for Haiti's second-largest city. Cap-Haïtien remains outside the active conflict zone concentrated in Port-au-Prince and Artibonite, though the GSF's geographic concentration in the capital leaves the northern city without international security coverage if violence expands further.

title: Day 14: MSF Cité Soleil Hospital Closure Persists; 30,000+ Displaced Since May 10; UN Formal Warning Active — 300,000 Commune Residents Without Emergency Care
detail: As of May 23, 2026, MSF's hospital in Cité Soleil — the only emergency health facility accessible to the approximately 300,000 people living in the commune under total gang control — entered its 14th consecutive day of closure with no announced reopening timeline. The hospital was evacuated on May 10 following intense intra-Viv Ansanm gang fighting between Chen Mechan/Taliban/400 Mawozo and Duvivier/Pyè 6 factions over Cul-de-Sac Plain cargo extortion revenues. MSF had treated over 40 gunshot wound patients in 12 hours before evacuating; one MSF security guard was shot by a stray bullet. 800+ displaced civilians had sheltered inside the compound before closure. The Centre Hospitalier de Fontaine also evacuated 11 neonatal ICU newborns during the initial violence surge. The UN's formal warning on surging mass displacement — first reported by JURIST on May 22 — remains active, with approximately 30,000 people displaced since May 10 across the West Department. The Shalom Church displacement site in Delmas 33 continues to shelter over 2,000 persons, and WFP has reached 8,500 newly displaced with emergency food while nine WFP-supported schools serving approximately 12,000 students remain unable to resume meal distributions. The 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan ($880 million needed) remains only approximately 20% funded ($172 million secured), with USAID budget cuts deepening the shortfall. Haiti remains on the UN's list of six global hunger hotspots of highest concern — alongside Mali, Palestine, South Sudan, Sudan, and Yemen — through May–June 2026. Gang conditions in Cité Soleil continue to prevent MSF and other medical providers from safely accessing the commune.

media.caption: MSF forced to evacuate Cité Soleil hospital — Day 14 of closure; 300,000 commune residents without emergency care as 30,000+ remain displaced
